questions.q: What will come from the stump of Jesse?
questions.a: A shoot will come from the stump of Jesse, and a branch from his roots will bear fruit.

questions.q: What will rest on him?
questions.a: The Spirit of Yahweh will rest on him.

questions.q: What will the Spirit of Yahweh give him?
questions.a: The Spirit of Yahweh will give him wisdom and understanding, counsel and might, knowledge, and the fear of Yahweh.

questions.q: What will he be very happy to do?
questions.a: He will be very happy to obey Yahweh.

questions.q: What standard will he use to judge the needy and the poor?
questions.a: He will not judge by what his eyes see or his ears hear. He will judge with righteousness and decide fairly.

questions.q: What will he do to the wicked?
questions.a: He will kill them with the breath of his lips.

questions.q: What will equip him to rule well?
questions.a: His desire to do what is right and honest will equip him to rule well.

questions.q: Who will lead the wolf, the lamb, and the other animals?
questions.a: A little child will lead them.

questions.q: What will the lion eat?
questions.a: The lion will eat straw like the ox.

questions.q: What will babies do near the holes of poisonous snakes?
questions.a: Babies will play safely near the holes of poisonous snakes.

questions.q: How will the animals act differently?
questions.a: They will not harm or destroy anything on Yahweh’s holy mountain.

questions.q: Why will the animals not hurt or destroy?
questions.a: The animals will not harm or destroy anything because the earth will be full of the knowledge of Yahweh.

questions.q: Who will come to the root of Jesse for advice?
questions.a: The nations will come to him to get good advice, the way soldiers gather around a signal flag.

questions.q: On that day why will the Lord extend his hand?
questions.a: He will extend his hand a second time to gather the remnant of his people who are left in Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Shinar, Hamath, and the coastlands of the sea.

questions.q: Who will he gather from the four edges of the earth?
questions.a: He will gather the outcasts of Israel and the scattered people of Judah from the four edges of the earth.

questions.q: What will happen to those who are hostile to Judah?
questions.a: Those who are hostile to Judah will be cut off.

questions.q: What will happen between Ephraim and Judah?
questions.a: Ephraim will not envy Judah, and Judah will not be hostile to Ephraim.

questions.q: What will Ephraim and Judah do together?
questions.a: They will swoop down on the Philistine hills to the west and take the possessions of the people to the east. They will also conquer Edom and Moab, and the Ammonites will obey them.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do to the gulf of the sea of Egypt and the Euphrates River?
questions.a: Yahweh will turn the gulf of the Sea of Egypt into dry land, and he will divide the Euphrates River into seven streams for people to walk across.

questions.q: Why will Yahweh dry up the gulf of the sea of Egypt and divide the Euphrates River?
questions.a: He will do this so people can walk across it in sandals.

questions.q: What will there be for the remnant of his people who are in Assyria?
questions.a: There will be a highway for them to return home, like there was for Israel when they came up from Egypt.

commentary.text: The peaceful character of Christ's kingdom and subjects. (Is. 11:1-9) The conversion of the Gentiles and Jews. (Is. 11:10-16)

Is. 11:1-9 The Messiah is called a Rod, and a Branch. The words signify a small, tender product; a shoot, such as is easily broken off. He comes forth out of the stem of Jesse; when the royal family was cut down and almost levelled with the ground, it would sprout again. The house of David was brought very low at the time of Christ's birth. The Messiah thus gave early notice that his kingdom was not of this world. But the Holy Spirit, in all his gifts and graces, shall rest and abide upon him; he shall have the fulness of the Godhead dwelling in him, Col. 1:19; 2:9. Many consider that seven gifts of the Holy Spirit are here mentioned. And the doctrine of the influences of the Holy Spirit is here clearly taught. The Messiah would be just and righteous in all his government. His threatening shall be executed by the working of his Spirit according to his word. There shall be great peace and quiet under his government. The gospel changes the nature, and makes those who trampled on the meek of the earth, meek like them, and kind to them. But it shall be more fully shown in the latter days. Also Christ, the great Shepherd, shall take care of his flock, that the nature of troubles, and of death itself, shall be so changed, that they shall not do any real hurt. God's people shall be delivered, not only from evil, but from the fear of it. Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? The better we know the God of love, the more shall we be changed into the same likeness, and the better disposed to all who have any likeness to him. This knowledge shall extend as the sea, so far shall it spread. And this blessed power there have been witnesses in every age of Christianity, though its most glorious time, here foretold, is not yet arrived. Meanwhile let us aim that our example and endeavours may help to promote the honour of Christ and his kingdom of peace.

Is. 11:10-16 When the gospel should be publicly preached, the Gentiles would seek Christ Jesus as their Lord and Saviour, and find rest of soul. When God's time is come for the deliverance of his people, mountains of opposition shall become plains before him. God can soon turn gloomy days into glorious ones. And while we expect the Lord to gather his ancient people, and bring them home to his church, also to bring in the fulness of the Gentiles, when all will be united in holy love, let us tread the highway of holiness he has made for his redeemed. Let us wait for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ unto eternal life, looking to him to prepare our way through death, that river which separates this world from the eternal world.
